questions.question: Q1 In the simulation, which scheduling algorithm produced the lowest average wait time for a mixed workload?

explanations.a: Incorrect. FIFO suffers from the convoy effect.
explanations.b: Correct. SJF minimizes average wait time by processing short jobs first.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Fair-Share balances fairness but may not minimize wait time.

questions.question: Q2 How does Kill/Restart compare to Checkpointing in terms of wasted compute?

explanations.b: Correct. All computational work is lost with Kill/Restart, while Checkpointing preserves progress.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Preemption always involves some waste.

questions.question: Q3 What happened when a high-priority emergency job was injected?

answers.a: It waited in the queue like other jobs
answers.b: Lower-priority jobs were preempted to free resources

explanations.b: Correct. The scheduler evicted lower-priority jobs to immediately allocate resources.

questions.question: Q4 Why did FIFO show poor GPU utilization with a mixed workload?

answers.a: Because it ran too many jobs simultaneously
answers.b: Because large jobs blocked the queue while resources sat idle
answers.c: Because it used too much memory
answers.d: Because it processed jobs too quickly

explanations.b: Correct. The convoy effect caused small jobs to wait while resources could not be efficiently packed.

questions.question: Q5 The formula W_avg = Σ(T_execution - T_submission) / Total Jobs measures:

answers.b: Average time each job spent waiting before execution

explanations.b: Correct. It calculates the mean waiting time across all completed jobs.

questions.question: Q6 What is a practical disadvantage of SJF scheduling?

answers.a: It is too simple to implement
answers.b: Long-running jobs may experience starvation (indefinite waiting)

explanations.b: Correct. Large jobs are perpetually deferred if short jobs keep arriving.

questions.question: Q7 How does cluster utilization change when switching from Kill/Restart to Checkpointing?

answers.b: Utilization increases because less work is repeated

explanations.b: Correct. Checkpointing reduces wasted cycles, improving effective utilization.

questions.question: Q8 In the simulation, what percentage of GPU time was wasted under Kill/Restart preemption with frequent evictions?

answers.c: A significant portion (often 20%+ depending on eviction frequency)

explanations.a: Incorrect. Frequent kills waste substantial compute.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The waste is typically higher.
explanations.c: Correct. Frequent kills cause significant waste as jobs restart from zero.

questions.question: Q9 Which combination provides the best balance of wait time and fairness?

explanations.a: Incorrect. FIFO has the convoy effect.
explanations.b: Incorrect. SJF can starve long jobs.
explanations.c: Correct. Fair-Share ensures equitable resource distribution while checkpointing preserves progress.

questions.question: Q10 What is the key engineering lesson from this experiment?

answers.a: FIFO is always the best scheduling choice
answers.b: Scheduling algorithm and preemption strategy critically affect cluster efficiency and user experience

explanations.b: Correct. The right combination of scheduling and preemption is essential for efficient cluster operations.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Scheduling is essential for shared resources.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Preemption is necessary for priority handling.
